sources.title: Properties of Admissible Symbolic Sequences in a Second Order Digital Filter with Overflow Nonlinearity
sources.reviewed: Abstract, introduction and Section 2, PDF pages 5-7. PDF page 6 inspected as a rendered image, including equations 1-6 and Figure 1.
sources.finding: Piecewise-affine overflow filter and symbolic region coding are established. The reviewed map is not a demonstrated nonlinear equivalent of the RAAR maps.
sources.limit: Not a complete paper or proof audit. Copyrighted PDF is held in the external reading directory, not redistributed in this repository.

sources.title: On Chaos in Digital Filters: Case b = -1
sources.reviewed: Abstract and Section 2 through the statement of Theorem 1, PDF pages 5-8. PDF pages 6-7 inspected as rendered images; equation and half-open interval conventions checked visually.
sources.finding: The branch formula is (y,-x+a*y+2*s) with an integer selector, hence a constant branch Jacobian. This supplies an exact comparison class, not a claim that every quantized model is affine.
sources.limit: The report's chaos classification proof was not fully audited. Copyrighted PDF is held externally and not redistributed.

sources.title: Application of Non-Linear Analysis Techniques to Sigma-Delta Modulators
sources.reviewed: Web-retrieved text of PDF pages 1-4: introduction, spectral and geometric analysis, nonlinear dynamics and references.
sources.finding: Affine regions, switching, parabolic trajectories and chaotic modulators predate this survey.
sources.limit: Equation 2 extraction is unreliable; no exact band-pass equation equivalence is claimed. Screenshot retrieval timed out. Direct local download failed certificate validation, so no local source hash or visual figure review is available.

own_mathematical_comparisons: Nonconstant trace of a regular RAAR branch excludes ambient affine conjugacy on an open set to ordinary piecewise-affine maps. Does not exclude nonlinear or invariant-set equivalence.
An explicit admissible attracting circle of two-cycles explains the numerical terminal behavior of sphere Case 1790. No historical priority is asserted for this elementary construction.
